lesson.butterfly_observation_study.title: Observational Butterfly
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.summa: Study the butterfly's center, wing contours, vein directions and edge texture to make a more observational drawing.
Observe the narrow body first, then add a few simple segment bands to establish its rhythm.
Compare the body height to the full page before adding wing shapes. Keep the mass centered.
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.compl: The body gives you a stable reference for the wing proportions.
Shape the upper wings with a broader top curve and a controlled return toward the body.
Watch the change of direction near each outer tip instead of trying to copy every tiny edge.
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.compl: The upper contours now carry most of the butterfly's silhouette.
Add the hindwings underneath and compare their width and drop to the upper pair.
Keep the hindwings visibly smaller and let their lower edge turn back toward the body.
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.compl: The full silhouette has a clearer natural proportion.
Place a few major vein directions from the center outward instead of drawing every line you can imagine.
Look for direction families: some veins rise toward the upper tip while others spread sideways or down.
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.compl: A small vein network adds structure without making the wings noisy.
Finish with a few restrained paired edge marks where the contour changes direction.
Use texture selectively. Empty space helps the detailed marks feel more intentional.
lesson.butterfly_observation_study.compl: Your observational butterfly is complete: refined contour, proportion and selected detail.
